text:
ellie: Heads up — noticed a ~$42k discrepancy between the AWS Marketplace payout for Q4 reserved capacity and our internal committed usage report. filing here so we can triage.

sam: can you paste the two totals? AWS statement vs our internal ledger.

ellie: AWS statement shows `Paid to seller: $234,120.00` for marketplace reseller SKUs. Our billing export (commitments.csv) shows `$276,140.00` credited to reseller accounts.

rob: that direction of mismatch (our ledger higher) usually means either duplicate invoice ingestion or a reseller rebate we haven't applied. did you pull the raw statement line items?

ellie: pasted the CSV lines from AWS statement (redacted):
```
InvoiceLineItemId,ProductCode,UsageStart,UsageEnd,Amount
inv-az-001,redwood.reserved.gpu,p1q23,2026-01-01,2026-01-31,125000.00
inv-az-002,redwood.marketplace.resell_fee,2026-01-01,2026-01-31,2340.00
inv-az-003,redwood.reserved.gpu,p2q23,2026-02-01,2026-02-28,107780.00
```

jia: quick sanity check — our usage export groups by commitment contract id. Can you share the commitment ids that sum to 276k?

ellie: commitment ids: C-9872 (125k), C-9901 (90k), C-9920 (61,140) => totals to 276,140.

nate: infra note — some Dedicated capacity moved from us-east-1 to us-east-2 mid-month (Jan). Marketplace SKUs are region-tagged. If our ledger rolled up both regions into a single commitment, we might be double-counting cross-region transfers.

sam: good catch. AWS Marketplace billing is per-Listing/region unless reseller mapping is configured. rob, did ingestion map regions to commitments correctly when we imported the marketplace CSV?

rob: the ingestion pipeline maps `ProductCode` -> `commitment_id` using a fuzzy lookup table maintained in `billing-mappings.yml`. I see an old entry mapping `redwood.reserved.gpu` -> C-9872 and a fallback that attaches unknown region rows to C-9901. Might explain C-9920 being an orphan.

ellie: I also noticed GCP reseller statement shows a vendor credit that we applied to commitments but AWS didn't have an equivalent. Could be cross-cloud offset misapplied.

luis: from sales side — C-9920 was a reseller pass-through for a partner in EMEA. Partner usage was billed via GCP reseller in Jan and AWS only billed infra hours. We expected a marketplace credit to offset partner payout. Did accounting apply that credit?

rob: there is a `marketplace_adjustments` table in the ledger. Query shows a GCP credit of -$61,140 applied on 2026-02-05 with memo `partner-resell-credit`. Looks like that was applied against the commitment but AWS payout never reflected it.

billing-bot: Automated note — we received an invoice dispute acknowledgment from AWS Marketplace on 2026-02-12 (case #AWSMKT-88321). Status: under review.

jia: action plan: 1) match each AWS InvoiceLineItemId to our commitment mapping (region + listing). 2) check if ingestion fallback assigned AWS region rows to GCP commitments. 3) reconcile partner credit entries in `marketplace_adjustments` and make sure they only apply to GCP-sourced invoices.

sam: priority: medium-high. This affects reserved capacity true-up for Feb billing. Nate, can infra produce a per-instance mapping of instance IDs that moved regions (east-1 -> east-2) with timestamps? We need to confirm whether a relocated instance triggered a new marketplace SKU line.

nate: will export `instance_migrations.csv` by EOD with instance_id, old_region, new_region, migration_ts. Quick note — migrations performed with live migration tool keep the same license/sku only if the Marketplace listing is shared across regions. Our GPU reserved listings are region-scoped, so expect duplication.

ellie: i'll extract the raw AWS CSV for Jan/Feb and attach to the accounting ticket. rob, once you confirm ingestion mapping I'll run a corrected import to see if totals align.

rob: also proposing to add one more rule to `billing-mappings.yml`: prefer exact region match, fall back to `unassigned-marketplace` instead of a commitment id. That will surface orphans for manual review instead of auto-assigning.

luis: good idea. we should also notify the partner finance contact about the delay — they'll ask why payout looks different. I'll draft a short note once we have root cause.

sam: ok team — owners: jia (reconciliation script), nate (migration export), rob (mapping + reimport), ellie (collect raw statements + cross-cloud credit audit). Check back with updates here. :thumbsup:

ellie: starting with the AWS raw CSV now. attaching partial snippet here for quick eyes:```
InvoiceLineItemId,LineDescription,Region,Amount
inv-az-001,"Reserved GPU hours us-east-1",us-east-1,125000.00
inv-az-003,"Reserved GPU hours us-east-2",us-east-2,107780.00
inv-az-004,"Marketplace reseller fee",us-east-1,2340.00
```

sam: noted. If the reimport still shows >$10k gap after mapping changes, escalate to AWS Marketplace support and request a detailed breakdown by listing-id and marketplace-transaction-id.

rob: will try local reimport tonight and post diff. if anyone sees weird duplicates in the import logs search for `WARN: fallback mapping used` — that's the smoking gun.

jia: I'll start the matching script now and ping when I have the first pass.

ellie: thanks all, will keep thread updated.
